headers.comment: HTML is never cached, so a reload always picks up the current ?v= stamps. This is the hinge: the HTML decides which asset versions load, so it has to be the one thing that is always fresh.

Assets are immutable because their URLs carry a content hash (scripts/stamp-assets.js). A changed file gets a new ?v= and therefore a new URL, so a year-long cache can never serve a stale one. Before the stamps existed these were max-age=3600 with unversioned URLs, which let a browser hold a cached data.js against a freshly fetched app.js for an hour after every deploy — app.js called a constant its data.js did not have yet, and the view rendered blank. Skew was invisible in testing because a hard refresh fixes it.
Fonts and images are content-stable but unstamped — a day is a fair trade.
